## Where streaming is implemented

**Core SSE engine** — `src/core/streaming.ts`
- `class Stream<Item>` — the base async-iterable wrapper around a `fetch` `Response`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` (`src/core/streaming.ts:35`) — parses a `Response` as Server-Sent Events, decoding via `_iterSSEMessages`/`SSEDecoder`, JSON-parsing each `data:` payload, and throwing `APIError` on embedded error events.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — parses a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used to "resume" a stream from a raw body, e.g. after `.toReadableStream()`).
- `_iterSSEMessages()` / `iterSSEChunks()` / `SSEDecoder` — low-level SSE framing, splitting on double newlines and `field: value` lines.
- Depends on `src/internal/decoders/line.ts` (`LineDecoder`, `findDoubleNewlineIndex`) for byte-to-line decoding.

**Wiring point (routes any request into the Stream)** — `src/internal/parse.ts`, `defaultParseResponse()` (line ~30):
```ts
if (props.options.stream) {
  if (props.options.__streamClass) {
    return props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(response, props.controller, client, ...);
  }
  return Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, props.controller, client, ...);
}
```
This is the single chokepoint: whenever a request is made with `stream: true`, the HTTP layer hands the raw `Response` to `Stream.fromSSEResponse` (or a custom subclass named in `options.__streamClass`).

**Higher-level, stateful stream wrappers** built on top of `Stream`, all extending `src/lib/EventStream.ts` (`EventEmitter`-style `.on()`/`.once()`/`.emitted()`/`.done()` API plus `AsyncIterable`):
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — accumulates `ChatCompletionChunk`s into a final `ChatCompletion`; `_fromReadableStream` calls `Stream.fromReadableStream` internally (line ~401).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — same, plus automatic tool-call execution loop.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — accumulates Assistants API run/thread events; also uses `Stream.fromReadableStream` (line ~170).
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — accumulates `ResponseStreamEvent`s into a final `Response` via `accumulateResponse` (`ResponseAccumulator.ts`); its `_createOrRetrieveResponse` (line ~167) calls `client.responses.create({...params, stream: true})`, which itself returns a raw `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` from the core engine, then iterates it.

**Separate mechanism (not SSE at all)**: `src/realtime/websocket.ts` (`OpenAIRealtimeWebSocket`, extends `OpenAIRealtimeEmitter` in `src/realtime/internal-base.ts`) implements bidirectional streaming over a raw `WebSocket`, independent of `core/streaming.ts`.

## Public API methods that route into it

| Method | File | Return type |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-122` | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | same file, ~142-168 | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | same file, ~201-206 | `ResponseStream` (calls `ResponseStream.createResponse`) |
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79` | `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | same file, ~221-226 | `ChatCompletionStream` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools({stream: true})` | same file, ~195-215 | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create(threadId, {stream: true})` (deprecated) | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-82` | `APIPromise<Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` | same file, ~161-234 | `AssistantStream` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs(id, {stream:true})` / `.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file, ~244-300 | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` / `AssistantStream` |
| `new OpenAIRealtimeWebSocket(...)` / `OpenAIRealtimeWS.create(...)` | `src/realtime/websocket.ts` | WebSocket-based emitter (distinct mechanism) |

## Not verified
- I did not read `src/resources/beta/realtime/*` or `src/resources/beta/chatkit/*` for any additional streaming entry points.
- I did not verify `src/internal/decoders/line.ts` contents in detail (only inferred its role from imports/usage).
- I did not check whether `azure.ts`/`bedrock.ts` client variants alter the streaming path (they likely just reuse the same `core/streaming.ts`, but I didn't confirm).
- Did not check `src/resources/audio/*` (e.g., transcription streaming) or `containers`/`evals` resources for possible additional `stream: true` usages beyond the three main families above.
